headline: Nuclear and organellar genome assemblies in algae and a moss expand lineage sampling
label: Algal And Bryophyte Genome Resources
summary: Assemblies of a nitroplast-hosting haptophyte and a moss, plus zygnematophycean phylogenomics, expand genomic sampling of photosynthetic eukaryotes.
synthesis: The dominant thread across these items is expanded genomic sampling of understudied photosynthetic eukaryotes. The Braarudosphaera bigelowii preprint assembles a 472.1-Mb nuclear genome together with organellar genomes for a nitroplast-hosting haptophyte and reports remodeling of nitrogen metabolism around the nitrogen-fixing organelle. The Warnstorfia fluitans preprint presents a 725 Mb de novo moss assembly with 30,421 predicted genes and chloroplast and mitochondrial genomes. The zygnematophycean study is phylogenomic rather than assembly-based, analyzing 104 transcriptomes (43 newly sequenced) across 2243 loci to resolve deep genetic structure and ancient radiations among the closest algal relatives of land plants. What is new is the pairing of organellar genomes with nuclear assemblies and of lineage-level sampling with phylogenetic context. The assembly preprints carry this thread most directly; the published phylogenomic study contributes comparative framing.
